task.name: A dev call the provider refuses without consuming tokens is recorded as cost-unknown, and the unverifiable budget skips unrelated stories
task.story_text:
## Observed

`forge sprint --verbose --issues 2775,2906,2908 --budget 50 --parallel 3` on
`release/v0.16`, forge `0.16.0rc15`. One story's dev call was refused by the
provider before any tokens were consumed. All three stories ended without work.

```
15:30:15.758 [issue-2775] ▸ DEV   gpt-5.4  iter=1
15:30:21.131 [issue-2775]   [DEV] FAIL | exit=1 | cost=unknown | output=321 chars
15:30:21.131 [issue-2775]   [DEV] error output: {"type":"error","status":400,
             "error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"The 'gpt-5.4'
             model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."}}
15:30:21.131 [issue-2775]   ✗ DEV   unknown  5s
15:30:21.199 [issue-2775] ✗ ESCALATE   Dev agent failed (exit=1) and produced no
             commits ahead of base — escalating to avoid an empty-diff APPROVE
15:30:22.810 ✗ issue-2775   unknown (>= $0.35 measured)  7m 8s
15:30:32.104 SKIPPED issue-2906 (budget unverifiable (spend unmeasured for 1
             source(s) [issue-2775]; measured $0.35 of $50.00 cap is a lower
             bound, so the cap cannot be verified; unresolved: issue-2775:
             measured $0.35, at most $37.93 more (story_allocation;
             run_id=8554de14250f, phase=DEV, role=dev,
             profile=openai-gpt-5.4-cli); to proceed, rerun with
             --accept-unmeasured-spend issue-2775))
15:30:32.120 SKIPPED issue-2908 (budget unverifiable ... same source ...)
```

The refused call lasted five seconds, returned 321 characters, and produced no
token usage because the provider rejected the request outright rather than
serving it. Forge recorded that as `cost=unknown`, then treated the story's
entire remaining allocation — `at most $37.93 more` — as possibly-spent. With
$50.00 of cap unverifiable, the two other stories were skipped before starting.

`issue-2906` and `issue-2908` were independent of `issue-2775`, shared no
dependency edge with it, and never dispatched an agent. The measured spend for
the whole sprint was $0.35.

The same rejection occurred in a separate repository eight minutes earlier
(`15:22:03`, a single-story run) and cost only that story, because there were no
siblings for the unverifiable budget to reach.

## Expected

A rejection issued before generation begins is a cost of zero, and must be
recorded as zero rather than as unknown. When a provider refuses a request
outright — an immediate, zero-token rejection such as an unsupported-model 400 —
nothing was generated and nothing was billed, and the transport can tell that
apart from a call that ran and whose accounting was lost. `cost=unknown` states
that the amount spent could not be determined; applying it to a request the
provider declined to serve asserts an uncertainty that does not exist.

This distinction is narrow on purpose. The absence of a usage block is not by
itself proof that nothing was spent — a completed call whose accounting was
dropped looks the same in that one respect, and must keep being treated as
genuinely unmeasured. What separates the two is an explicit pre-generation
refusal from the provider. Only that class resolves to zero; everything else
remains unknown and continues to constrain the run's budget exactly as it does
today, because a cap that cannot be verified is still a cap that must be
respected.

The operator-facing outcome must name what actually happened. Stories reported as
failed or skipped for budget reasons, when the cause was a single unusable model
and the measured spend was $0.35 against a $50.00 cap, describe a budget problem
that did not exist and hide the one that did. Where a story is withheld because
another story's spend could not be established, the report names which story,
which phase and which model produced the unmeasurable amount.

Scope note: withholding a rejected model from further selection, so later stories
route elsewhere instead of meeting the identical refusal, is routing behavior and
belongs to fuzzypete/theforge#2914. This issue is the cost classification only.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `eca4d4307cb05337c0b5cdd858f2916a63cf3958` captured at `2026-09-05T18:52:16.676754+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/sprint/unmeasured.py` — `sha256:deb0574b6770bc405887240523b55d3eb56b370d7133e55b62f521e3a6f486d4`
- `src/theforge/sprint/budget.py` — `sha256:dd61188737848ee35fb67c62108d1899f9db93f2b3f52471a7e1cba61e5f150d`
- `src/theforge/runners/cli.py` — `sha256:040b383fa370fe99ceadbd37e09bec380360b2a57d74f912c15d47bf04a8539a`
- `src/theforge/runners/runner_codex.py` — `sha256:cb910a2da214156688ebc36f7bdfbec58feb83391e4cbf97bba2e808e72dcdca`
- `src/theforge/runners/api.py` — `sha256:9f4ab646f101e376bfbce03f03d3133b192c9d99f55811af9e947422c58699c1`
- `tests/test_runner_codex.py` — `sha256:e858d03e2bc257541d5cb8a3071d5fae5a871f8b7f62929d8c0529e19ea28d19`
- `src/theforge/config/models.py` — `sha256:e55f3549db704cbebecf1f82e823c150ab846e05f935130361f00ef0aa47fb61`

### Observed symptom

A dev invocation via the Codex CLI transport (profile openai-gpt-5.4-cli) was
refused by the provider outright — a pre-generation HTTP 400
invalid_request_error ("The 'gpt-5.4' model is not supported when using
Codex with a ChatGPT account") — yet forge recorded the call's cost as
unknown rather than zero. Because that unknown could not be bounded to a
verified ceiling, the sprint-wide budget check failed closed, and two other
stories (issue-2906, issue-2908) that shared no dependency with the refused
story and never dispatched an agent were skipped as "budget unverifiable"
even though total measured sprint spend was $0.35 against a $50.00 cap.

### Reproduction / evidence

Evidence is the issue's attached verbose sprint log
(`forge sprint --verbose --issues 2775,2906,2908 --budget 50 --parallel 3`):
`[DEV] FAIL | exit=1 | cost=unknown | output=321 chars`, followed by
`SKIPPED issue-2906 (budget unverifiable ... unresolved: issue-2775: measured
$0.35, at most $37.93 more (story_allocation; ... phase=DEV, role=dev,
profile=openai-gpt-5.4-cli))`.

I reproduced the classification mechanism directly against the codebase at
HEAD (release/v0.16) with a Python REPL exercising
`theforge.runners.runner_codex`:
  - `_classify_codex_launch_failure(returncode=1, stdout='{"type":"error","status":400,"error":{...}}', stderr='')`
    → returns a launch-failure reason (would record measured $0.00) when the
    error line is the ONLY stdout content.
  - `_classify_codex_launch_failure(returncode=1, stdout='{"type":"turn.started"}\n{"type":"error","status":400,...}', stderr='')`
    → returns `None` (NOT a launch failure) once a `turn.started` event
    precedes the error line, because `_exited_before_any_turn` treats
    `turn.started`/`turn.failed` as proof "the model was engaged" regardless
    of whether the provider ever began generating tokens.
  - This matches `tests/test_runner_codex.py::test_turn_failed_counts_as_a_started_turn`,
    which asserts exactly this behavior by design: "The model was engaged:
    unmeasurable, not free."
Codex CLI's real event stream for a turn does emit `thread.started`/
`turn.started` as soon as it begins processing a turn, before the first
request to the provider is validated — so an immediate model-rejection
(400 invalid_request_error, zero tokens) still passes through a
`turn.started` (or `turn.failed`) event and is disqualified from the
zero-cost classification, falling through to `_extract_codex_cost`, which
correctly finds no usage and returns `cost_usd=None` (COST_UNKNOWN).

### Hypotheses tested

- **[ruled out]** The sprint-level unmeasured-budget guard (src/theforge/sprint/budget.py, sprint/unmeasured.py) incorrectly propagates one story's unmeasured spend to unrelated sibling stories.
  - Evidence: budget.py's unresolved/unverifiable logic and unmeasured.py's per-source ceiling derivation operate correctly on the input they're given — a whole-sprint cap that cannot be verified because a NAMED source is unmeasured is fail-closed by design (comment in unmeasured.py: 'a ceiling that cannot be checked is not a ceiling'). This is the intended, sound behavior for a genuinely unmeasured call; the defect is upstream in what gets classified as unmeasured in the first place.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Read directly from the repository at HEAD.
- **[confirmed]** The Codex CLI transport's pre-turn launch-failure classifier (_exited_before_any_turn / _classify_codex_launch_failure in runner_codex.py) treats any turn.started/turn.failed event as proof the model was engaged, so an immediate zero-token provider rejection that occurs after a turn.started event is misclassified as cost-unknown instead of measured $0.00.
  - Evidence: Direct execution against the repository's runner_codex.py at HEAD shows _classify_codex_launch_failure returns None (disqualifying zero-cost classification) once a turn.started event precedes the error event — even though the error is an immediate, pre-generation 400 invalid_request_error with no token usage. tests/test_runner_codex.py::test_turn_failed_counts_as_a_started_turn asserts this is the current, deliberate design: any turn.failed is unconditionally routed to unmeasurable, never free.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Reproduced against HEAD by calling the real functions; the test file's assertion is independent confirmation of the current code's intended behavior, not a restatement of this issue (it predates #2913 and encodes a design decision about upstream-500-style failures, not about immediate model-rejection 400s).
- **[unverifiable]** The OpenAI raw-API transport (runners/api.py) has the same defect for a 400 invalid_request_error.
  - Evidence: api.py re-raises HTTP 400 exceptions for caller-side fallback handling (line ~377) rather than running them through the codex-specific turn-activity classifier; the observed incident's profile (openai-gpt-5.4-cli) is the CLI/codex transport, not the API transport, so this path was not exercised by the reported symptom and its cost-classification behavior on a 400 was not traced end-to-end.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Partial reading only; recorded as a related, out-of-scope observation rather than ruled in or out.

### Confirmed cause

In src/theforge/runners/runner_codex.py, the Codex CLI transport's
pre-turn/launch-failure classifier (`_exited_before_any_turn`, used by
`_classify_codex_launch_failure`) disqualifies a run from the zero-cost
"launch failure" classification the instant it sees a `turn.started` or
`turn.failed` event anywhere in stdout, on the theory that such an event
proves "the model was engaged." Codex CLI emits `turn.started` as soon as it
begins processing a turn — before the provider has validated or begun
generating against the request — so a provider's immediate, pre-generation
rejection (an HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error`, e.g. an unsupported model)
still carries a `turn.started`/`turn.failed` pair and is routed past the
launch-failure check into the normal cost-extraction path
(`_extract_codex_cost`), which correctly finds no token usage and returns
`cost_usd=None` — i.e. COST_UNKNOWN — rather than the true measured $0.00.
That single-story cost-unknown then becomes an unresolved, unbounded source
in the sprint's unmeasured-spend accounting, and the sprint-wide budget
check (which is functioning correctly by refusing to verify a cap against an
unbounded unknown) skips unrelated sibling stories as a consequence.

Support: Direct execution of the real functions from src/theforge/runners/runner_codex.py
at HEAD against a stdout string modeled on the observed error
(`{"type":"error","status":400,"error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"The 'gpt-5.4' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."}}`)
shows `_exited_before_any_turn` returns `False` and
`_classify_codex_launch_failure` returns `None` once a `turn.started` event
precedes the error line — which is what a live Codex CLI turn produces even
for an immediately-rejected request. This is corroborated by
tests/test_runner_codex.py::test_turn_failed_counts_as_a_started_turn, which
is a prior assertion of the current design intent ("The model was engaged:
unmeasurable, not free") for the general case of an upstream failure (e.g.
"upstream 500") — a case correctly left cost-unknown — but the same
unconditional rule also swallows the narrower, distinguishable case this
issue is about: a pre-generation 400 rejection that never reached generation
at all.
Support provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. The classifier behavior was observed directly by invoking the real functions in a Python shell against src/theforge/runners/runner_codex.py at HEAD. The cited test (test_turn_failed_counts_as_a_started_turn) is read as documentation of intended current behavior, not as independent proof — it predates and does not mention this issue.
Independence note: This text uses independence/corroboration language. Verify the cited material is a second source rather than a prior assertion.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/runners/runner_codex.py:
  - `_TURN_ACTIVITY_EVENT_TYPES` (~line 418) includes `turn.started` and
    `turn.failed` unconditionally.
  - `_exited_before_any_turn` (~line 435) treats any event of those types as
    proof a turn began, with no way to distinguish "provider began
    generating" from "provider immediately rejected the request before
    generation."
  - `_classify_codex_launch_failure` (~line 486) and its call site in
    `_run_codex` (~lines 849-874), which decide whether a completed codex
    invocation is billed as measured $0.00 (launch failure) or falls through
    to `_extract_codex_cost` and is recorded COST_UNKNOWN.

### Fix-success criterion

When a Codex CLI dev/review invocation is rejected by the provider before
any generation occurs — specifically an immediate, pre-generation refusal
such as an HTTP 400 invalid_request_error for an unsupported model, distinct
from a completed-but-unparseable call — the resulting AgentResult must carry
cost_usd=0.0 (measured), not cost-unknown. A genuinely unmeasurable failure
(e.g. an upstream 500, a timeout, or any case where token usage cannot be
ruled out) must continue to be recorded cost-unknown exactly as today. As a
result, a sprint whose only unmeasured source is such a pre-generation
refusal must not skip unrelated sibling stories for "budget unverifiable,"
and the operator-facing report must correctly attribute the failure to the
refused model rather than to an apparent budget shortfall.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- Whether the raw OpenAI API transport (runners/api.py) has the same or a different cost-classification gap for an immediate 400 invalid_request_error was not traced end-to-end; it re-raises 400s for caller-side handling rather than running the codex-specific turn-activity classifier, so its behavior on a rejected model may differ.
- Routing an already-rejected model (e.g. gpt-5.4 under a ChatGPT-account Codex login) away from future story dispatch, so later stories in the same sprint don't hit the identical refusal, is explicitly scoped to fuzzypete/theforge#2914 per the issue text and is not part of this cost-classification fix. (related: fuzzypete/theforge#2914)

### Advisory repair proposal

> Advisory only: this is an unverified repair idea from the investigation, not part of the confirmed diagnosis contract.

Consider distinguishing a `turn.failed` event that carries a
pre-generation-shaped provider error (e.g. `error.status == 400` and
`error.error.type == "invalid_request_error"`, no `usage` block anywhere in
the stream) from a `turn.failed` that could plausibly have consumed tokens
(e.g. upstream 5xx, timeout, no explicit "this request was never valid"
signal). Only the former should be treated as a zero-cost, not-yet-engaged
turn. This likely means splitting `_exited_before_any_turn`'s "turn began"
proof into two tiers, or adding a narrowly-scoped pre-generation-refusal
detector alongside it, rather than changing the blanket
`_TURN_ACTIVITY_EVENT_TYPES` membership (which the existing
"upstream 500"/"usage limit reached" tests correctly rely on staying
cost-unknown).

### Notes

I did not have access to a live Codex CLI to directly confirm that a
real invocation against an unsupported model emits `turn.started` before
the rejection error (as opposed to, in some cases, exiting with no stdout
activity at all, which would already be correctly classified as measured
$0.00 by the existing launch-failure path). This is inferred from Codex
CLI's documented event-stream behavior (turn.started begins as soon as
the turn is dispatched) and from the fact that the issue's own observed
behavior (cost=unknown, not measured $0.00) is only reproducible in the
code at HEAD when a turn-activity event precedes the error — the
no-activity-at-all case already produces the correct zero-cost outcome.
The raw OpenAI API transport (runners/api.py) was not traced end-to-end for
the same defect and is recorded only as a related, unverified concern.
